name: coda_upcall
prose: Real function is coda_upcall(vcp, inSize, outSize, buffer) (the slice only contains its prototype, the body is later in upcall.c). Precondition: the caller does not hold vcp->vc_mutex; buffer is a complete input message of inSize bytes allocated by the caller (alloc_upcall) with a valid inputArgs header; outSize is NULL for an asynchronous request or points to an int holding the expected reply size (0 meaning inSize) for a synchronous one. Postcondition: takes vcp->vc_mutex and releases it before returning (for a synchronous request coda_waitfor_upcall drops and re-takes the mutex while sleeping, so it is not held continuously during the wait). If vcp->vc_inuse is 0 it returns -ENXIO and if the request structure cannot be allocated it returns -ENOMEM, in both cases with nothing queued and buffer still owned by the caller. Otherwise it stamps buffer->ih.unique with ++vcp->vc_seq, queues the request on vcp->vc_pending and wakes Venus. If outSize is NULL it returns 0 at once; the request now owns buffer, which the caller must not free (it is freed after Venus reads it). If outSize is non-NULL it waits (coda_waitfor_upcall, which ends only when Venus replied (CODA_REQ_WRITE), the request was aborted (CODA_REQ_ABORT) or a signal is pending): if Venus replied it sets *outSize to the reply size and returns -(reply result) (0 on success, the negated Venus error otherwise); in every other case it returns -EINTR, including when the request was aborted by Venus shutdown (the code returns -EINTR there even though a comment mentions ENODEV) and when the wait ended without a pending signal (a warning is logged); when the wait ended because of a pending signal after Venus had read the request (and the request was not aborted) it additionally queues a CODA_SIGNAL message at the head of the pending list, but returns -ENOMEM instead of -EINTR if that signal request (or its message buffer) cannot be allocated, and queues nothing if Venus has since died (vc_inuse is 0). If the signal interrupted the wait before Venus read the request nothing is queued. In all synchronous cases the request structure is freed here and buffer remains owned by the caller (it holds the reply when one arrived).
note: Reviewer wrong: coda_upcall returns -EINTR on CODA_REQ_ABORT (fs/coda/upcall.c:773-777 'error = -EINTR; if ((req->uc_flags & CODA_REQ_ABORT) || !signal_pending(current))'); the ENODEV text is only a comment (l.~755). Prose tightened: vc_mutex is dropped inside coda_waitfor_upcall while sleeping.

name: ceph_lock
prose: Real function name is ceph_lock(file, cmd, fl) (the packet name ceph_fcntl does not exist in the source; the slice cuts the head of ceph_lock, so the name is absent from the slice). Precondition: file is an open ceph file, fl a valid file_lock, cmd an fcntl lock command (F_GETLK, F_SETLK or F_SETLKW style); the caller holds no ceph locks. Postcondition: it returns -ENOLCK if FL_POSIX is not set in fl->c.flc_flags and -ESTALE if the inode is shut down, in both cases with no side effects. The operation is GETFILELOCK for F_GETLK and SETFILELOCK otherwise, and a local wait flag is set for F_SETLKW (also when the lock is an unlock). While holding ci->i_ceph_lock briefly it reads CEPH_I_ERROR_FILELOCK; if set it returns -EIO (before that, for a SETFILELOCK-type unlock it calls posix_lock_file(file, fl, NULL) to drop the local lock and ignores its result). For a SETFILELOCK unlock it then calls try_unlock_file, which temporarily adds FL_EXISTS and calls locks_lock_file_wait: only when that returns -ENOENT does ceph_lock return early (0 if the caller had not set FL_EXISTS, -ENOENT if it had) and nothing is sent to the MDS; for any other local result, success or another error, try_unlock_file returns 1 and the function continues. It then calls ceph_lock_message (CEPH_LOCK_FCNTL, the lock type derived from fl as shared, exclusive or unlock); that function forces wait to 0 for unlock requests and for GETFILELOCK, so the MDS request waits only for a non-unlock SETLKW. For SETFILELOCK ceph_lock_message first sets fl->fl_ops to the ceph lock ops and increments i_filelock_ref and takes an inode reference (igrab) through fl_copy_lock (both released later by fl_release_private), whether or not the request then fails; ceph_lock_message additionally takes its own inode reference (ihold) for the MDS request, held until that request is put, and does not take it if the request cannot be created. If ceph_lock_message fails its negative error is returned. If it succeeds for GETLK, 0 is returned with fl filled in from the MDS reply; if it succeeds for a SETFILELOCK whose fl->c.flc_type is not F_UNLCK, the lock is also applied locally with posix_lock_file: if that fails a CEPH_LOCK_UNLOCK ceph_lock_message is sent to undo the remote lock (its result ignored) and the posix_lock_file error is returned; otherwise 0 is returned.
note: Reviewer wrong: ceph_lock_message calls fl->fl_ops->fl_copy_lock(fl, NULL) (locks.c:~79-80) = ceph_fl_copy_lock (atomic_inc i_filelock_ref + igrab, locks.c:~35-40), before any request creation; it also ihold()s the inode for the request (~l.89). Added the ihold sentence.

name: afs_update_volume_creation_time
prose: Precondition: op is a valid afs_operation whose pre_volsync.creation (old) and volsync.creation (new) hold the creation times before and after the operation; volume is a valid afs_volume (volume->servers non-NULL); the caller holds no lock this function takes. Postcondition: returns 0 and sets volume->creation_time = new, without anything else, if volume->creation_time was TIME64_MIN; returns 0 changing nothing if new equals the current creation_time or if the current creation_time (cur) differs from old (another operation already advanced it). Otherwise (cur == old and new != cur): for an RW volume, and for a Backup volume when new < old, it does atomic_inc(&volume->cb_scrub), emits the creation-regress trace, sets volume->creation_time = new and returns 0. For a Backup volume with new >= old it does atomic_inc_return(&volume->cb_ro_snapshot), emits the vos-release trace, sets volume->creation_time = new and returns 0. For any other (RO) volume it first calls afs_is_server_excluded(op, volume). That helper takes the RCU read lock and scans volume->servers for op->server; it treats the server as excluded (returns 1 at once) if the server is flagged AFS_SE_EXCLUDED in that list and also if op->server is not found in the list at all (or the list is empty), since the default is excluded. Otherwise it sets AFS_VOLUME_NEEDS_UPDATE on the volume and calls afs_check_volume_status(op->volume, op) (which may sleep and refresh the volume status from the VL server, and may itself set or clear that flag), returning its negative errno if that fails, else the result of repeating the scan on the possibly refreshed server list (0 if the server is present and not excluded, 1 if excluded or absent). If the helper returns a negative errno, this function returns it, leaving cb_scrub, cb_ro_snapshot and creation_time unchanged, but AFS_VOLUME_NEEDS_UPDATE may have been set and the volume status may have been updated. If it returns a positive value it emits the volume-excluded trace and returns that value, with creation_time and the counters unchanged. If it returns 0 (server present and not excluded) the RO volume takes the same path as the Backup new >= old case: atomic_inc_return(&volume->cb_ro_snapshot), vos-release trace, creation_time = new, return 0. No lock or reference is left held. Increments are plain atomic increments (not a cmpxchg); the guard against races is the cur == old test.
note: Reviewer right: __afs_is_server_excluded initialises is_excluded = true and only changes it when op->server is found (validation.c:~160-176), so absent server => 1 from the helper (twice). Prose corrected.

name: _badblocks_set
prose: Precondition: bb points to an initialized struct badblocks whose page table is valid; the caller must not hold bb->lock (the function takes the write seqlock itself with interrupts saved); s and sectors give the range and acknowledged says whether new entries are acknowledged. Postcondition: returns false, without taking the lock or changing anything, if bb->shift < 0 (badblocks disabled) or sectors == 0. Otherwise (note the rounddown/roundup calls under bb->shift are statement expressions whose results are discarded, so s and sectors are NOT rounded) it takes the write seqlock and repeatedly inserts, merges, combines or overwrites entries for [s, s+sectors), advancing s and shrinking sectors by the length handled each pass (a pass may also skip over a range that is already recorded with ack state that cannot be overwritten). It stops early, with only part of the range (possibly none) recorded, when the table is full or when a front overwrite would need extra table slots (extra > 0) that cannot be had; it then returns false. If the whole range is processed it also tries to combine with the following entry (try_adjacent_combine) and returns true. The return value is exactly (remaining sectors == 0). If at least one entry was added or merged (added != 0) it calls set_changed(bb) and, if acknowledged is 0, sets bb->unacked_exist = 1, else calls badblocks_update_acked(bb). bb->count is updated for every insertion, combine or overwrite. The write seqlock is released (interrupt flags restored) on every path that took it.
note: include/linux/math.h:71-90: roundup and rounddown are statement-expression macros that yield a value and do not assign; badblocks.c:860-861 discard it, so s and sectors are unchanged. Rest of _badblocks_set re-verified line by line (badblocks.c:852-979).

name: btrfs_replace_file_extents
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the inode lock and has locked the file range [start, end] (end inclusive); path is a usable (empty) path in the inode's root; extent_info is NULL (hole punch) or describes the replacement extent; trans_out is a valid output pointer. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, changing nothing and without touching any reservation, if end <= start. Otherwise it initialises a temporary block reservation, starts a transaction (reserving 3 items, or 2 when the NO_HOLES feature is set and extent_info is NULL) and drops every file extent overlapping [start, end], possibly over several transactions: the drop loop repeats only when btrfs_drop_extents returns -ENOSPC, in which case it commits progress and ends the transaction before starting a new one. In each such pass: when extent_info is NULL the inode byte count is decreased by the bytes found, and the dropped part is replaced by hole items for the part below the rounded-up i_size, or merely cleared from the extent range map for the part at or past it; when extent_info is given and the drop end is beyond extent_info->file_offset a piece of the replacement extent is inserted and extent_info->data_len, data_offset and file_offset are advanced past it; the inode is then updated (i_version bumped and, when extent_info is NULL or extent_info->update_times, mtime/ctime set). When extent_info is NULL the loop also skips over any part already covered by a hole (find_first_non_hole). After the loop (which was left normally or by an error) and when no error is pending, it fills the remainder with holes (extent_info NULL, below rounded i_size, nonempty range) or clears the range from the extent range map (extent_info NULL, past i_size), and when extent_info is non-NULL it inserts the rest of the replacement extent (btrfs_insert_replace_extent with the remaining data_len); this post-loop insertion exists after the slice shown. Once the drop loop has been entered, if extent_info is non-NULL and not a new extent the inode is marked for a full fsync, even when the function goes on to fail; that does not happen for the -EINVAL return, nor when the first start-transaction or reservation-migrate fails before the loop. Returns 0 on success, with *trans_out set to the live transaction, which the caller must end. On failure it returns a negative errno (from starting a transaction, migrating the block reservation, dropping extents, filling holes, clearing the range, inserting the replacement extent, updating the inode, or finding the next non-hole), aborts the transaction for drop errors other than -ENOSPC (except -EOPNOTSUPP when no new extent is being inserted) and for fill_holes, clear-range, insert-replace and inode-update errors (in the loop and after it); start-transaction, reservation-migrate and find_first_non_hole errors do not abort. On failure any live transaction is ended by the function and *trans_out is left unset. Once the reservation has been initialised, it is released before every return.
note: Reviewer wrong: post-loop replacement insertion exists at fs/btrfs/file.c:2584-2591 (if (extent_info) btrfs_insert_replace_extent(... extent_info->data_len ...)), after the slice end 2583. Corrected: full_sync only once the loop is entered (set before 'if (ret) goto out_trans' after the loop; not for -EINVAL/start/migrate failure).

name: handle_cap_grant
prose: Precondition: handle_cap_grant(inode, session, cap, grant, xattr_buf, extra_info): the caller holds session->s_mutex, ci->i_ceph_lock, and (for a CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT grant) session->s_mdsc->snap_rwsem for reading; cap belongs to inode (the auth cap or, for a non-import grant, possibly a non-auth cap), grant is a decoded mds caps message, xattr_buf is the buffer holding the xattr blob (used only if a newer xattr version is accepted), and extra_info holds the decoded ancillary data. Postcondition: returns void; it releases ci->i_ceph_lock and session->s_mutex on return and, if grant->op is IMPORT, also releases snap_rwsem (read). While under the lock: if the cap generation was stale, cap->issued and cap->implemented are reset to CEPH_CAP_PIN; if the message seq is not newer than cap->seq the cap's seq and its issued caps are retained (newcaps |= cap->issued); cap->cap_gen is set to the current session generation and cap->seq to the message seq; mode/uid/gid, nlink, xattr blob (taking a ref on xattr_buf and dropping the old blob when version is newer), times, dir stats, layout (the replaced old pool_ns is returned to the caller through extra_info->pool_ns), file size/truncate state, max_size on the auth cap, and inline version are updated from the grant according to which caps (newcaps) and extra_info->issued allow; cap->issued becomes newcaps (kept within cap->implemented, which only gains bits; BUG_ON otherwise). A revocation of cached or buffered caps may queue writeback or invalidation and set CEPH_I_FLUSH_FORCE when a revoke ack must be deferred; a revoke op otherwise clears cap->mds_wanted and forces a flush ack. After unlocking it may fill inline data, queue vmtruncate/writeback/invalidate, invalidate aliases for a deleted inode (nlink 0), wake ci->i_cap_wq waiters, and finally, after s_mutex has been released, call ceph_check_caps when check_caps was set (auth cap only, or all caps, always with CHECK_CAPS_NOINVAL, plus CHECK_CAPS_FLUSH_FORCE when the op is a revoke whose ack was not deferred).
note: Reviewer wrong: fs/ceph/caps.c:3534 comment 'caller holds s_mutex and i_ceph_lock, we drop both'; mutex_unlock(&session->s_mutex) at 3868; up_read(&session->s_mdsc->snap_rwsem) in the IMPORT branch at 3843; spin_unlock(&ci->i_ceph_lock) just after; __releases at 3542-3543.

name: affs_readdir
prose: Precondition: file is an open AFFS directory whose private_data points to a valid struct affs_dir_data (allocated by affs_dir_open); ctx->pos is 0 or 1 for the start, or encodes the resume position as ((hash_pos << 16) | chain_pos) + 2 (hash_pos is not checked against the hash table size before the first table lookup, so a ctx->pos with hash_pos at or beyond s_hashsize reads outside the table); the caller holds the usual directory read serialisation (inode lock shared); may sleep. Postcondition: if ctx->pos < 2 it sets data->ino to 0 and emits "." and ".." with dir_emit_dots, returning 0 immediately (before taking the directory lock, without updating data->cookie) if that emit fails. It then takes the AFFS directory lock, which is released before return on every path after that. A chain_pos of 0xffff logs a warning and moves ctx->pos to the start of the next hash bucket (this update of ctx->pos stays even if a later step fails). If the directory header block cannot be read it returns 0 after unlocking, emitting no further entries and not updating data->cookie or data->ino in this stage; note that in the same call the dots may already have been emitted and data->ino already reset to 0 by the ctx->pos < 2 step. If data->ino is non-zero and the directory inode version equals data->cookie it resumes directly at block data->ino; otherwise it walks chain_pos entries of the chain of bucket hash_pos; a failed block read during this walk is logged, the directory header buffer is released and the function returns -EIO, again without updating data->cookie or data->ino in this stage (data->ino may still have been reset to 0 earlier in the same call if the dots were emitted). If the chain has fewer entries it continues with the following non-empty hash buckets, setting ctx->pos to the start of each new bucket. Entries are emitted with dir_emit(name, namelen, block number, DT_UNKNOWN) and ctx->pos is incremented per emitted entry; if dir_emit returns false the emission stops (ctx->pos is not incremented for the refused entry). A failed read of an entry block while emitting is logged and only ends the current chain (emission continues with the next non-empty bucket). When emission ends normally or by a dir_emit refusal, data->cookie is set to the current inode version and data->ino to the current chain variable ino: the block number of the entry that was refused (0 when everything was emitted; after an unreadable entry block it is that block's number unless a later non-empty bucket was processed). All buffer heads are released. The return value is 0, or -EIO only for the failed block read while skipping to the resume position in the chain.
note: Reviewer right: fs/affs/dir.c:96-98 sets data->ino=0 and emits dots before the header read at ~108 (failure goes to out_unlock_dir, 0). Also hash_pos from ctx->pos indexes table[] unchecked at 121. Prose rewritten.

name: create_elf_fdpic_tables
prose: Real function create_elf_fdpic_tables(bprm, mm, exec_params, interp_params) in fs/binfmt_elf_fdpic.c (the head is in the previous slice, so the name is not in this slice; the earlier name create_elf_fdpic_stack_layout does not exist). Precondition: bprm, mm, exec_params and interp_params are valid, exec_params->loadmap is populated, interp_params->loadmap is NULL or populated. The argument strings (bprm->argc of them) followed by the environment strings (bprm->envc) are in the exec argument area: with an MMU they are already on the user stack starting at bprm->p; without an MMU they are still in the holding pages bprm->page[] and mm->start_stack must be the user stack top (this function copies them onto the stack itself, see below). Postcondition: with an MMU the stack pointer starts at arch_align_stack(bprm->p); without an MMU it starts at mm->start_stack and transfer_args_to_stack copies the strings from the holding pages onto the user stack (lowering sp, adjusting bprm->exec) and sp is aligned down to 16. The function returns 0 after writing onto the user stack, below those strings: the ELF_PLATFORM and ELF_BASE_PLATFORM strings if the architecture defines them, the exec load map and, if interp_params->loadmap is non-NULL, the interpreter load map, the auxiliary vector, the NULL-terminated envp[] and argv[] pointer arrays and argc; and after setting exec_params->map_addr, interp_params->map_addr (only if an interpreter load map exists), current->mm->context.exec_fdpic_loadmap and interp_fdpic_loadmap (the latter only if present), the auxiliary vector copy in mm->saved_auxv, mm->arg_start (bprm->p with an MMU; mm->start_stack - (MAX_ARG_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE - bprm->p) without, using the start_stack value before this function overwrites it), arg_end, env_start, env_end and finally mm->start_stack = the final 16-byte-aligned stack pointer. Returns -EFAULT if transfer_args_to_stack fails (non-MMU), if any copy_to_user fails, or if any put_user of an argv[]/envp[] entry, a terminating NULL or argc fails. Returns -EINVAL if, while filling argv[] or envp[], strnlen_user returns 0 (the string cannot be read) or a length greater than MAX_ARG_STRLEN (no terminating NUL within that limit); an empty string (length 1) is accepted and causes no error. An internal consistency check BUG_ON(csp != sp) halts the kernel if the computed stack layout is inconsistent. On failure the user stack and some mm and params fields may be partly updated (for example map_addr is set before the load map is copied; mm->saved_auxv is filled before it is copied out); no lock or reference is acquired and nothing is freed.
note: Reviewer right: binfmt_elf_fdpic.c:~523-529 (non-MMU) sp = mm->start_stack; transfer_args_to_stack(bprm,&sp) < 0 -> -EFAULT; fs/exec.c:731-756 copies holding pages onto the stack and adjusts bprm->exec. Precondition rewritten for both MMU/non-MMU.

name: btrfs_find_allocatable_zones
prose: Precondition: device is a zoned device with a non-NULL zone_info; hole_start and num_bytes are multiples of the zone size (both ASSERTed, which is a no-op unless assertions are enabled); hole_end is not required to be aligned or to be at least hole_start. Postcondition: returns a u64 position; it takes no lock, acquires no reference and modifies nothing. Starting at pos = hole_start, while pos < hole_end it considers the region of nzones = num_bytes / zone size zones starting at the zone of pos (bytes [pos, pos + num_bytes)). If the region would extend beyond the last zone of the device (end zone index > nr_zones) the function returns hole_end immediately; that value is returned as is and is not guaranteed to be zone-aligned. If the zone at pos is sequential and the nzones zones of the region are not all marked empty, pos advances by one zone and the search continues (when the zone at pos is conventional the emptiness of the zones is not checked). Otherwise, for each of the BTRFS_SUPER_MIRROR_MAX mirrors in order, if the region overlaps that mirror superblock-log zones (BTRFS_NR_SB_LOG_ZONES zones) pos moves to the start of the first zone after that log; else if the byte range [pos, pos + num_bytes) overlaps the regular superblock copy of that mirror (BTRFS_SUPER_INFO_SIZE bytes) pos moves to the zone-aligned position after that copy; either way the search then continues with the new pos. If the region overlaps none of them the loop stops and pos is returned. The result is therefore one of: hole_start itself, unchanged, if hole_start >= hole_end (the loop body never runs); hole_end (device too small, possibly unaligned); the first candidate position that satisfies the conditions; or, when the loop ran off the end of the hole, a position at or beyond hole_end reached by the last advance (the caller must compare the result against hole_end). Every return value other than the early hole_end is zone-aligned (hole_start is aligned by the precondition and pos only changes by whole zones, zone starts, or ALIGN to the zone size).
note: zoned.c:1079-1121: while (pos < hole_end) never runs when hole_start >= hole_end, so return pos (line 1121) returns hole_start unchanged; prose now lists it. Early return hole_end at 1084; all other results zone-aligned.

name: create_pending_snapshot
prose: Precondition: trans is a running transaction handle in the commit phase, pending is an initialised pending-snapshot descriptor with non-NULL path and root_item (both asserted), and root, dir, dentry and readonly describe the source subvolume, parent directory and new name. Postcondition: the function always clears the pending state before returning: new_root_item is freed, pending->root_item and pending->path are set to NULL (the path is freed by its scope-based cleanup), the filename is freed if it was set up, and the skip-qgroup mark is cleared once it was set. Early failures (fscrypt_setup_filename, btrfs_get_free_objectid, reservation of the relocation metadata with btrfs_block_rsv_add when it is needed) store the errno in pending->error and return 0 (ret is still 0 at that point); an existing directory entry of the same name (found after the reservation switch described below) stores -EEXIST in pending->error and returns 0 after restoring trans->block_rsv and clearing trans->bytes_reserved. Otherwise it switches trans->block_rsv to the pending reservation and performs the snapshot: records the parent root in the transaction (a failure here is returned without aborting the transaction), picks the directory index, checks that the name does not exist, creates the qgroup (-EEXIST, and -ENOTCONN when quotas are disabled, are ignored), runs the delayed items, records the source root in the transaction, sets last_snapshot, copies the root item (readonly flag per pending->readonly, new uuid, parent uuid, otime), COWs and copies the root node, inserts the new root item and root ref, gets the new fs root into pending->snap, does the relocation accounting and, only in qgroup mode FULL or SIMPLE, the qgroup accounting or inherit step, inserts the directory item, updates the parent inode and adds the subvolume uuid and, if present, the received uuid to the uuid tree (-EOVERFLOW on the received-uuid insertion is turned into 0). On a failure after the reservation switch it sets pending->error to the errno and returns it; every such failure aborts the transaction except the failure to record the parent root, the qgroup accounting/inherit step and an -EEXIST from the received-uuid insertion, which are returned (and stored in pending->error) without an abort. On success it returns 0 and pending->error is 0. On all paths after the switch trans->block_rsv is restored and trans->bytes_reserved is cleared; pending->snap is not released here and stays set once btrfs_get_new_fs_root succeeded.
note: transaction.c:1662 int ret = 0; early failures only set pending->error (1676-1700) and reach free_pending/free_fname/clear_skip_qgroup with ret still 0, so they return 0; line 1736-1737: existing dir entry sets pending->error = -EEXIST then goto dir_item_existed (1927) with ret 0, so returns 0. Prose only reordered/clarified (qgroup mode, switch order).

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: Precondition: trans is the handle of a transaction of trans->fs_info, cur_trans = trans->transaction, and it is the only user of the handle (use_count == 1, only asserted). The function consumes the handle on every path (it is ended with btrfs_end_transaction, or freed here after the commit or in cleanup_transaction), so the caller must not use trans afterwards. Postcondition: it first clears BTRFS_FS_NEED_TRANS_COMMIT. Early exits that do not clean up the transaction (the handle is ended with btrfs_end_transaction, whose result is ignored, and the errno is returned): (a) if the transaction is already aborted the abort error is returned and nothing else is done; (b) otherwise btrfs_trans_release_metadata is called and trans->block_rsv is set to NULL; if this task is the one that sets BTRFS_DELAYED_REFS_FLUSHING it runs btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, 0) and on failure returns that errno without creating the pending block groups; then btrfs_create_pending_block_groups is called (void); and if this task is the one that sets BTRFS_TRANS_DIRTY_BG_RUN (tested and set under ro_block_group_mutex) it calls btrfs_start_dirty_block_groups and on failure returns that errno. Then, under trans_lock: if cur_trans->state is already at least COMMIT_PREP (another task is committing) it links the pending snapshot of trans, if any, into cur_trans->pending_snapshots with add_pending_snapshot, takes an extra reference on cur_trans, ends the handle with btrfs_end_transaction, waits until the transaction reaches COMPLETED (SUPER_COMMITTED when trans->in_fsync), then returns the abort error if cur_trans aborted, otherwise the result of btrfs_end_transaction, and drops the extra reference. Otherwise this task performs the commit: it sets state COMMIT_PREP; if cur_trans is not first in the transaction list and the previous transaction has not reached the wanted state it waits for it and fails with its abort error if that one aborted; if cur_trans is first in the list and the filesystem is in an error state (BTRFS_FS_ERROR) it fails with -EROFS; it sets COMMIT_START and records the start time of the critical section; it decrements the external writer count, calls btrfs_start_delalloc_flush (in this tree it only starts writeback when FLUSHONCOMMIT is set and returns 0, but its result is checked) and runs the delayed items (failure of either goes to the cleanup path); waits until there are no external writers; runs the delayed items again (failure goes to the cleanup path); waits for the delalloc flush (only with FLUSHONCOMMIT) and for pending ordered extents; pauses scrub; under trans_lock it links the pending snapshot (add_pending_snapshot) and sets COMMIT_DOING; waits until it is the only writer; clears BTRFS_FS_COMMIT_TRANS; and fails with the abort error if the transaction is aborted. It then takes reloc_mutex, creates the pending snapshots, runs the delayed items, runs all delayed refs, commits the fs roots, frees the log root tree, accounts qgroup extents, commits the cow-only roots, fails with the abort error if the transaction is aborted, switches the commit roots (cur_trans is re-read from fs_info->running_transaction), updates the super block copy, takes tree_log_mutex, sets UNBLOCKED with fs_info->running_transaction NULL, releases reloc_mutex, writes the btree (btrfs_write_and_wait_transaction; on failure btrfs_handle_fs_error is called, tree_log_mutex is dropped and it fails), writes the superblocks (a failure just fails, without btrfs_handle_fs_error), sets SUPER_COMMITTED, finishes the extent commit, sets the last committed transid and the state COMPLETED, removes the transaction from the list, puts two references on it, ends the freezable write section if applicable, resumes scrub, detaches the handle from the task if current, frees the handle and returns 0. Any failure after the commit was started (previous transaction aborted, -EROFS, delalloc flush, delayed items, abort, snapshot creation, or any later step up to finish_extent_commit) ends in the cleanup path: reloc_mutex is released if held, scrub is resumed if it had been paused, the reserved metadata, pending block groups and chunk metadata are released, trans->block_rsv is set to NULL, the warning "Skipping commit of aborted transaction." is logged, the handle is detached from the task, and cleanup_transaction aborts the transaction with that errno, removes it from the list and destroys it, drops its references, cancels scrub unless relocation is running, and frees the handle; the negative errno is returned. The pending snapshot of trans is linked into the transaction only by the two add_pending_snapshot calls described above; it is not linked on the early exits (aborted, delayed refs, dirty block groups) nor on failures before COMMIT_DOING (previous transaction aborted, -EROFS, delalloc flush, first or second delayed items).
note: transaction.c:2209 btrfs_commit_transaction: run_delayed_refs failure jumps to lockdep_trans_commit_start_release (2642) before btrfs_create_pending_block_groups (2245); btrfs_start_delalloc_flush (2143) returns 0 here, result checked at 2350; write_all_supers failure (2563) has no btrfs_handle_fs_error. Prose rewritten for the whole function.

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: Precondition: trans is the handle of a transaction of trans->fs_info, cur_trans = trans->transaction, and it is the only user of the handle (use_count == 1, only asserted). The function consumes the handle on every path (it is ended with btrfs_end_transaction, or freed here after the commit or in cleanup_transaction), so the caller must not use trans afterwards. Postcondition: it first clears BTRFS_FS_NEED_TRANS_COMMIT. Early exits that do not clean up the transaction (the handle is ended with btrfs_end_transaction, whose result is ignored, and the errno is returned): (a) if the transaction is already aborted the abort error is returned and nothing else is done; (b) otherwise btrfs_trans_release_metadata is called and trans->block_rsv is set to NULL; if this task is the one that sets BTRFS_DELAYED_REFS_FLUSHING it runs btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, 0) and on failure returns that errno without creating the pending block groups; then btrfs_create_pending_block_groups is called (void); and if this task is the one that sets BTRFS_TRANS_DIRTY_BG_RUN (tested and set under ro_block_group_mutex) it calls btrfs_start_dirty_block_groups and on failure returns that errno. Then, under trans_lock: if cur_trans->state is already at least COMMIT_PREP (another task is committing) it links the pending snapshot of trans, if any, into cur_trans->pending_snapshots with add_pending_snapshot, takes an extra reference on cur_trans, ends the handle with btrfs_end_transaction, waits until the transaction reaches COMPLETED (SUPER_COMMITTED when trans->in_fsync), then returns the abort error if cur_trans aborted, otherwise the result of btrfs_end_transaction, and drops the extra reference. Otherwise this task performs the commit: it sets state COMMIT_PREP; if cur_trans is not first in the transaction list and the previous transaction has not reached the wanted state it waits for it and fails with its abort error if that one aborted; if cur_trans is first in the list and the filesystem is in an error state (BTRFS_FS_ERROR) it fails with -EROFS; it sets COMMIT_START and records the start time of the critical section; it decrements the external writer count, calls btrfs_start_delalloc_flush (in this tree it only starts writeback when FLUSHONCOMMIT is set and returns 0, but its result is checked) and runs the delayed items (failure of either goes to the cleanup path); waits until there are no external writers; runs the delayed items again (failure goes to the cleanup path); waits for the delalloc flush (only with FLUSHONCOMMIT) and for pending ordered extents; pauses scrub; under trans_lock it links the pending snapshot (add_pending_snapshot) and sets COMMIT_DOING; waits until it is the only writer; clears BTRFS_FS_COMMIT_TRANS; and fails with the abort error if the transaction is aborted. It then takes reloc_mutex, creates the pending snapshots, runs the delayed items, runs all delayed refs, commits the fs roots, frees the log root tree, accounts qgroup extents, commits the cow-only roots, fails with the abort error if the transaction is aborted, switches the commit roots (cur_trans is re-read from fs_info->running_transaction), updates the super block copy, takes tree_log_mutex, sets UNBLOCKED with fs_info->running_transaction NULL, releases reloc_mutex, writes the btree (btrfs_write_and_wait_transaction; on failure btrfs_handle_fs_error is called, tree_log_mutex is dropped and it fails), writes the superblocks (a failure just fails, without btrfs_handle_fs_error), sets SUPER_COMMITTED, finishes the extent commit, sets the last committed transid and the state COMPLETED, removes the transaction from the list, puts two references on it, ends the freezable write section if applicable, resumes scrub, detaches the handle from the task if current, frees the handle and returns 0. Any failure after the commit was started (previous transaction aborted, -EROFS, delalloc flush, delayed items, abort, snapshot creation, or any later step up to finish_extent_commit) ends in the cleanup path: reloc_mutex is released if held, scrub is resumed if it had been paused, the reserved metadata, pending block groups and chunk metadata are released, trans->block_rsv is set to NULL, the warning "Skipping commit of aborted transaction." is logged, the handle is detached from the task, and cleanup_transaction aborts the transaction with that errno, removes it from the list and destroys it, drops its references, cancels scrub unless relocation is running, and frees the handle; the negative errno is returned. The pending snapshot of trans is linked into the transaction only by the two add_pending_snapshot calls described above; it is not linked on the early exits (aborted, delayed refs, dirty block groups) nor on failures before COMMIT_DOING (previous transaction aborted, -EROFS, delalloc flush, first or second delayed items).
note: transaction.c btrfs_start_delalloc_flush (transaction.c:2143-2160) returns 0 always (try_to_writeback_inodes_sb only with FLUSHONCOMMIT); caller checks ret and goes to lockdep_release. Prose made explicit about the checked result and rewritten for the whole function.

name: ceph_readdir
prose: Precondition: file is an open ceph directory file (file->private_data is its struct ceph_dir_file_info), ctx is a valid dir_context and the caller holds the inode lock of the directory for iteration as usual for iterate; no ceph spinlocks are held. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if CEPH_F_ATEND is set. Otherwise it first emits "." (pos 0) and ".." (pos 1), advancing ctx->pos to 1 and 2; if dir_emit refuses one of them (caller buffer full) it returns 0 with ctx->pos left at that entry position. It then returns the negative errno of ceph_fscrypt_prepare_readdir if that fails (a positive return of it is ignored). It touches the write file mode under i_ceph_lock. If the dcache can be used (mount option DCACHE set, NOASYNCREADDIR not set, not a snapdir, directory complete and ordered, shared file cap issued) it calls __dcache_readdir and returns its result unless that is -EAGAIN, in which case it falls through. Normal path: when the buffered reply (dfi->last_readdir) does not cover ctx->pos it drops the previous reply and sends a READDIR (or LSSNAP) request to the auth MDS for the current frag, returning -errno on failure of request creation (PTR_ERR), reply-buffer allocation, kzalloc of r_path2 (-ENOMEM), encoding of the encrypted last name, or the request itself (in each case the request reference taken here is dropped), or the note_last_dentry error (after dropping the reply). The reply is then kept in dfi->last_readdir. It emits the buffered entries from ctx->pos onward, setting ctx->pos to each entry offset before dir_emit and incrementing it after a successful emit; it returns -EIO (after dropping the reply: dfi->last_readdir becomes NULL) if an entry offset is below ctx->pos or an entry has no inode; if dir_emit refuses an entry it returns 0 with ctx->pos at that entry offset and dfi->last_readdir retained (not dropped) so the next call resumes. When the buffered entries are exhausted the reply reference is dropped (last_readdir = NULL) and it moves on to further requests for the same frag or the next frag; at the end of the last frag it sets CEPH_F_ATEND and, if i_release_count still equals dfi->dir_release_count, marks the directory complete (and, only when dfi->dir_ordered_count also equals i_ordered_count, complete and ordered, setting i_size to the readdir-cache size), then returns 0. On every return no spinlock is held; a reply reference remains in dfi->last_readdir only if it was kept from an earlier request and not yet dropped (in particular after a full-buffer stop).
note: fs/ceph/dir.c:545-551: rde->offset < ctx->pos puts last_readdir, sets it NULL and returns -EIO (also 553-557 for a NULL rde->inode.in); dir.c:567-575: dir_emit refusal returns 0 without dropping last_readdir. The skipping of low offsets is in the binary search at 529-540 and in __dcache_readdir, not in this loop.

name: v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl
prose: Real function v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl(dir, dentry, file, flags, omode) in fs/9p/vfs_inode_dotl.c (the slice starts in its middle, after the lookup and O_CREAT checks; the function that is literally named v9fs_vfs_create_dotl is a different, 3-line wrapper that just returns v9fs_vfs_mknod_dotl(idmap, dir, dentry, omode, 0) and is not what the slice contains). Precondition: dir is a directory inode on a 9p mount, dentry is a dentry of the entry to open in it, file is the struct file being opened; the function may sleep. Postcondition, returns an int: if the dentry is in lookup state and v9fs_vfs_lookup returns a non-NULL result or leaves the dentry positive, it returns finish_no_open(file, res); otherwise, if O_CREAT is not set in flags, it returns finish_no_open(file, NULL); in neither case is anything created. Otherwise it creates and opens the file: gets the parent fid (v9fs_parent_fid), clones it (clone_fid) as the open fid ofid, computes the creation gid and the mode adjusted by the directory's default ACL (v9fs_acl_mode), converts the open flags to 9P flags (a write-only open is turned into read-write without append when the mount has CACHE_WRITEBACK), and sends Tlcreate (p9_client_create_dotl), then invalidates the directory's cached attributes, walks the parent fid to the new name to get an unopened fid, obtains a new inode from that fid (v9fs_get_new_inode_from_fid), sets the ACLs on it from the default ACL values, attaches the unopened fid to the dentry (v9fs_fid_add) and instantiates the dentry with the inode (d_instantiate), then calls finish_open(file, dentry, generic_file_open). On success (err 0) file->private_data is set to ofid, the fscache cookie is used (when CACHE_FSCACHE and CONFIG_9P_FSCACHE), the open fid gets its cache/mode flags and is added to the inode's open fid list (v9fs_open_fid_add), FMODE_CREATED is set in file->f_mode, and it returns 0. On failure it returns the negative errno of the first failing step (parent fid lookup, fid clone, ACL mode computation, p9_client_create_dotl, the walk, inode creation, or finish_open); it fails before instantiating the dentry in all cases except finish_open, after which the dentry is already instantiated with the new inode, and if the server-side create already succeeded the file still exists on the server. On every path after the create-checks, the parent fid, the open fid and the new fid are dropped with p9_fid_put unless they were handed over to the dentry or inode (which sets those pointers to NULL), and the ACL references are released with v9fs_put_acl.
note: fs/9p/vfs_inode_dotl.c:242-245: if (d_in_lookup) { res = v9fs_vfs_lookup(...); if (res || d_really_is_positive(dentry)) return finish_no_open(file, res); } so res may be NULL with a positive dentry and finish_no_open(file, NULL) is returned; with res NULL and a negative dentry control proceeds. The prose states exactly this (non-NULL result OR positive dentry).

name: resolve_indirect_refs
prose: Precondition: ctx, path and preftrees are valid; preftrees->indirect holds only indirect refs (none has ref->parent set); sc is NULL or a share-check context. Postcondition: allocates a local ulist of parents (returns -ENOMEM, nothing changed, if that fails). Then, while the indirect tree is not empty, it takes its first ref: if that ref has parent set (a bug) it warns and returns -EINVAL, leaving the ref in the indirect tree; otherwise it removes the ref from the indirect tree and decrements the tree count. A ref with count 0 is freed. If sc is set and the root_id of the ref differs from the root id of sc->root, the ref is freed and BACKREF_FOUND_SHARED (6, a positive value) is returned. Otherwise resolve_indirect_ref is called with the parents ulist. A result of -ENOENT is tolerated: the unresolved ref is inserted into the direct tree as is. Any other non-zero result (negative errno such as -ENOMEM, -EIO, -EUCLEAN, other tree search errors, or a positive value from the callee) frees the ref and is returned. On a zero result the ref itself receives the first parent of the ulist (0 if the ulist is empty) and that parent inode list; for every further parent a new prelim_ref is allocated (-ENOMEM after freeing the current ref if that fails), copied from the ref with its own parent and inode list, and inserted into the direct tree; the ref itself is inserted into the direct tree last (it may be merged or freed there). The ulist is then reinitialised (the inode lists now belong to the refs) and the loop goes on. Returns 0 if the whole indirect tree was consumed. On an early return the refs not yet taken stay in the indirect tree. On every return (success or failure) free_leaf_list frees the parents ulist and the inode lists attached to its nodes at that moment, including, after a failure part-way, lists already attached to refs inserted in the direct tree in the same iteration.
note: fs/btrfs/backref.c:702-710 free_leaf_list frees unode_aux_to_inode_list(node) for every node and nothing in resolve_indirect_refs (730-830) clears node->aux; ulist_reinit (820) is only reached on success; error paths (772, 779, 796-801) free the ref with free_pref (212, kmem_cache_free only) and fall to out: free_leaf_list(parents) at 828.

name: btrfs_split_extent_map
prose: Real function btrfs_split_extent_map(inode, start, len, pre, new_logical) in fs/btrfs/extent_map.c (the slice starts after the head, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: 0 < pre < len (asserted); the inode's extent map tree holds an uncompressed, non-logging extent map of length len that overlaps [start, start + len), has a real disk_bytenr, is PINNED and is on the inode's modified extents list (its list head is not empty); these conditions are asserted. The caller must not already hold the io_tree extent lock on that range or em_tree->lock, since the function takes both. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM, with nothing locked or changed, if either of the two new extent maps cannot be allocated; otherwise it locks the range [start, start + len) in inode->io_tree, takes em_tree->lock for writing and looks the map up; if no extent map is found it returns -EIO leaving the tree unchanged. On success it returns 0 after replacing the old map by two maps that carry the old map's flags (including PINNED, captured before the flag is cleared on the old map) and generation and are inserted as modified: [em->start, em->start + pre) mapped to new_logical, and [em->start + pre, em->start + len) mapped to the old map's block start plus pre (the results of replace_extent_mapping and add_extent_mapping are not checked). The reference taken by the lookup inside this function and the tree's reference on the old map are dropped. On every path after both new maps were allocated, including the -EIO and the success path, it releases the write lock and the range lock and drops this function's own allocation reference on both new extent maps: on success the two inserted maps stay alive through the reference the tree took on insertion, on -EIO they are freed; if the second allocation fails the first map is freed.
note: extent_map.c:1108-1114 out_unlock/out_free_pre: btrfs_free_extent_map(split_mid) and (split_pre) run on every path, including success; inserted maps survive via refcount_inc in setup_extent_mapping (465). Prose said only uninserted maps are freed.

name: replay_one_extent
prose: Precondition: wc->trans is a running transaction, wc->root is the subvolume root being replayed with a log root, wc->log_leaf, wc->log_slot and wc->log_key identify an EXTENT_DATA item in the log tree, and wc->subvol_path is released on entry. Postcondition: for an extent type other than REG, PREALLOC or INLINE it aborts the log replay and returns -EUCLEAN; if the inode cannot be read (btrfs_iget_logging) it aborts the replay and returns that error. Otherwise, if the subvolume already has an identical REG/PREALLOC file extent item at the same offset, it does nothing more and returns 0 (a negative result of the initial btrfs_lookup_file_extent is not checked: it is treated like "not found"). Else it drops the extents overlapping [start, extent_end) (extent_end = start + num_bytes, or the sector-aligned end for an inline extent) with btrfs_drop_extents; an inline extent is then overwritten with overwrite_item; a hole with the NO_HOLES feature is only accounted; for other items the file extent item is inserted into the subvolume tree, an explicit hole needs nothing more, and a real extent is qgroup-traced, then either referenced (btrfs_inc_extent_ref) if it already exists in the extent tree or allocated (btrfs_alloc_logged_file_extent) if not, and the checksums covering it are read from the log root, the existing checksums of that range are deleted from the csum tree and the logged ones added. Finally the file extent range [start, extent_end) is recorded in the inode, the inode byte count is updated by the extent size and the dropped bytes, and the inode item is updated. It returns 0 on success, or the negative errno of the failing step, each of which also aborts the log replay with a message (overwrite_item aborts internally before returning its error). The inode reference taken is dropped (iput) on every return after it was obtained, and the temporary checksum list is freed.
note: Reviewer wrong: btrfs_lookup_csums_list (file-item.c:643-646, out: label) kfree()s every entry already added to the list when it returns <0, so replay_one_extent has nothing left to free after the abort at tree-log.c 'failed to lookups csums'; the later while(!list_empty) loop frees all entries on the success and delete/add-failure paths. Rest of prose re-checked against tree-log.c replay_one_extent (extent type check, iget, lookup, drop_extents, inline overwrite_item, NO_HOLES, insert, qgroup trace, ref/alloc, csums, update_inode, out: iput).

name: btrfs_recover_log_trees
prose: Precondition: called during mount with log_root_tree the log root tree of the filesystem, on a filesystem being mounted read-write, with no other log replay in progress. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM at once if the path cannot be allocated. Otherwise it sets BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING, starts a transaction on the tree root (a failure is returned after cleanup), pins all blocks of the log root tree, and then walks all log roots (TREE_LOG_OBJECTID root items, from the highest offset downward) in the stages pin, replay inodes, and replay everything: for each log root it reads the log tree and looks up the subvolume root with the same id; if the subvolume root does not exist (-ENOENT) the log's root block is pinned and the log is skipped; otherwise the log root is attached to the subvolume root, the root is recorded in the transaction, the log tree is walked, and in the final stage the inode link counts are fixed up and the root's free objectid is re-initialised. Temporary root references (the log root and the subvolume root) are dropped for each log. After the last stage the path is freed, the transaction is committed (which unpins the blocks) and, if the commit succeeded, BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING is cleared and 0 is returned; if the commit fails its error is returned and the flag stays set. On any error before the commit (walk_log_tree, btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_read_tree_root, btrfs_get_fs_root other than -ENOENT, btrfs_pin_extent_for_log_replay, btrfs_record_root_in_trans, fixup_inode_link_counts, btrfs_init_root_free_objectid) the transaction is aborted (not when starting it failed), the transaction handle is ended if one was started, the log root reference is put, BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING is cleared, the path is freed and the negative errno is returned.
note: Reviewer wrong: tree-log.c:7820-7824 'ret = btrfs_commit_transaction(trans); if (ret) return ret;' returns directly; clear_bit(BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING) at 7826 runs only after a successful commit. The error: label (clear_bit) is reached only from the pre-commit failures. Rest of prose re-checked.

name: btrfs_get_old_root
prose: Precondition: root is a btrfs root and time_seq is a sequence number registered with the tree modification log. Postcondition: it read-locks the current root node and takes a reference on it (btrfs_read_lock_root_node). If tree_mod_log_oldest_root finds no root modification at or after time_seq it returns that very node, still read-locked and referenced, and the caller owns both. Otherwise the current root node (eb_root) is read-unlocked and its reference dropped on every remaining path (before the old root block is read, before the dummy buffer is allocated, or after the clone is made), and a different extent buffer eb is built. If the oldest relevant modification is a root replacement (BTRFS_MOD_LOG_ROOT_REPLACE), the logical address and level of the old root and the generation of the replace entry are taken from it and tree_mod_log_search is called for the old root's logical address; otherwise the search is made for the current root node's own start address. Three cases follow. (1) Root replaced and the search found an entry that is not a BTRFS_MOD_LOG_KEY_REMOVE_WHILE_FREEING entry: the old root block is read from disk (a read error or a not up-to-date block is logged with WARN_ON and a warning and NULL is returned), read-locked, cloned, then the log is searched again for the same address while the old block is still locked, after which the old block is read-unlocked and released; if the second search finds nothing or an entry older than the first (ASSERTs also check this) the clone is freed and NULL is returned, otherwise the second entry replaces the first. (2) Root replaced but the search found no entry or found a KEY_REMOVE_WHILE_FREEING entry: a dummy extent buffer at the old root's logical address is allocated (the entry found, if any, is still used for the rewind below). (3) Root not replaced: the current root node is cloned. NULL is returned if the clone or the dummy allocation fails. For a replaced root the header of eb is set to bytenr = eb->start, backref revision MIXED, the level of the old root, the generation of the replace entry, and the owner: the owner of the current root node in case (2), and 0 in case (1). eb is then read-locked; if a log entry was found (tm non-NULL) the operations after time_seq are rewound on it with tree_mod_log_rewind, and if none was found it only warns (WARN_ON) when the level of eb is not 0. It also warns if the item count exceeds the maximum node pointers. The caller must btrfs_tree_read_unlock and free_extent_buffer a non-NULL result; when NULL is returned no lock or reference taken by this function remains held.
note: Reviewer right: tree-mod-log.c:1049-1060 second tree_mod_log_search runs before btrfs_tree_read_unlock(old)/free_extent_buffer(old). Also the dummy-buffer branch (else if (old_root), line 1068) is taken when no entry is found OR the entry is KEY_REMOVE_WHILE_FREEING (1036), and tm stays set for the rewind. Owner: eb_root_owner is 0 in the read-old-block case (initialised at 1014), set only in the dummy case.

name: ext4_ext_insert_extent
prose: Real function ext4_ext_insert_extent(handle, inode, path, newext, gb_flags) (the slice begins in the middle of it; the packet suffix '(tail; name elided in excerpt)' is not part of the name). Precondition: handle is an active journal handle with enough credits, path is the path returned by ext4_find_extent for the logical block of newext (valid down to the leaf at ext_depth(inode)) and is owned by the caller, newext points to a valid extent to insert whose block range does not overlap an existing extent, and gb_flags holds EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_* flags. Postcondition: returns a struct ext4_ext_path * or an ERR_PTR. On success the returned path (which may be a different path from the one passed in: the old one is then freed, e.g. when the next leaf or a newly created leaf is used) is owned by the caller, and newext has been merged with an adjacent extent (unless gb_flags has EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO, which skips merging) or inserted in sorted position in the leaf, eh_entries incremented, the indexes above corrected and the leaf buffer marked dirty (ext4_ext_dirty). On failure it returns ERR_PTR(err) and the caller must not use or free the path it passed in: -EFSCORRUPTED if newext has actual length 0 or path[depth].p_hdr is NULL (after EXT4_ERROR_INODE), or the error of ext4_ext_get_access, ext4_find_extent (looking for the next leaf), ext4_ext_create_new_leaf (e.g. -ENOSPC; it returns the error path itself), ext4_ext_correct_indexes or ext4_ext_dirty; except that for the create-new-leaf failure the path is as released by that function. The in-memory extent leaf may already have been modified when a late step (index correction or dirtying) fails.
note: Reviewer wrong: ext4/extents.c:2025 'if (ex && !(gb_flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO))' wraps the whole append/prepend merge block, and extents.c:2204 skips ext4_ext_try_to_merge under PRE_IO, so PRE_IO skips all merging. Failure paths re-checked (errout frees path; ext4_ext_create_new_leaf frees path itself on error).

name: radix_sort
prose: Precondition: array and array_buf each point to at least num valid struct bucket_item entries (array_buf is scratch of the same size, distinct from array) and num >= 1 (array[0].count is read unconditionally). Postcondition: returns nothing. Let max count be the largest array[i].count and bitlen = ALIGN(ilog2(max count), 8), computed in a u64 and then stored in an int. For a max count of 2 or more bitlen is the floor of log2 of the max count rounded up to a multiple of 8 (at least 8). If the max count is 1, ilog2 is 0 and bitlen is 0; if the max count is 0, ilog2(0) is -1 which is converted to u64 before the alignment, so the ALIGN wraps around to 0 (this is relied on only as observed behaviour of the code). When bitlen == 0 no pass runs: array and array_buf are left completely unchanged. Otherwise array_buf is overwritten with intermediate results (contents unspecified on return) and the entries of array are rearranged (a permutation of the same items, no entry lost or duplicated) by a stable LSD radix sort using 4-bit digits (two passes per loop iteration, so the last pass writes back into array; bitlen is a multiple of 8, so the number of passes is even) over the low bitlen bits of count, with each digit inverted so that larger digits come first. Entries are therefore ordered by (count mod 2^bitlen) in non-increasing order, ties keeping their original relative order; the bits at position bitlen and above are not examined. Consequently, if every count is below 2^bitlen the result is sorted by count in non-increasing order (this always holds when the max count is below 256, and it holds for max count 1 trivially). If some count is 2^bitlen or more the order is by the low bits only and need not be sorted by count (for example counts 256 and 1 end up as 1, 256); it can still happen to be sorted (counts 257 and 256 end up as 257, 256). No lock, reference or allocation is involved.
note: compression.c:1337-1345: bitlen=ALIGN(ilog2(max),8), only bits below bitlen are examined. Reviewer right that 'fully sorted only if every count < 2^bitlen' was false (257,256 ends sorted); now: guaranteed sorted when all counts < 2^bitlen, else ordered by count mod 2^bitlen (256,1 -> 1,256), may coincide with sorted. Added max count 0 wrap behaviour.

name: __ceph_setattr
prose: Real function __ceph_setattr(idmap, inode, attr, cia) in fs/ceph/inode.c (the slice is its middle part, so the name is not in the slice; the wrapper ceph_setattr is a different function outside this slice). Precondition: inode is a ceph inode, attr says which attributes to change (ia_valid), cia is NULL or carries an fscrypt_auth buffer owned by the caller, and the caller holds the inode lock. Postcondition: it finds an alias dentry with d_find_alias and, if there is one, builds its path and checks MDS access for MAY_WRITE; if that check returns -EACCES the function returns -EACCES at once with nothing changed; any other failure to build the path or check access, or having no alias, only sets do_sync (no local application under exclusive caps) and continues. At the label retry it allocates a cap flush (-ENOMEM if that fails) and creates a SETATTR MDS request (its error is returned, after freeing the cap flush, if creation fails). Under i_ceph_lock it reads the issued caps; if the inode has no head snap context and caps include an EXCL cap or FILE_WR it takes mdsc->snap_rwsem for reading (re-reading the caps if i_ceph_lock had to be dropped to wait for it). If cia->fscrypt_auth is set: when its length is larger than the allowed size, or when CONFIG_FS_ENCRYPTION is off, it returns -EINVAL after dropping i_ceph_lock and putting the request and cap flush, without releasing snap_rwsem if it was taken, and without changing cia->fscrypt_auth; otherwise it either installs the buffer in the inode (when !do_sync and AUTH_EXCL is issued; the old buffer is freed) or, if AUTH_SHARED is not issued or the stored value differs, puts it in the request (and requests release of AUTH_SHARED), or does nothing with it if the stored value is identical and AUTH_SHARED is issued; in all three cases it then sets cia->fscrypt_auth to NULL. For each of ATTR_UID, GID, MODE and ATIME it applies the change to the inode locally when !do_sync and the matching EXCL cap (AUTH_EXCL for uid, gid and mode; FILE_EXCL for atime) is issued and records the dirtied cap; for atime (and mtime) a newer value is also applied locally under FILE_WR when !do_sync; otherwise, if the shared cap is not issued or the value differs, the value goes into the request and its mask, with the shared caps to release; ATTR_MODE in that request branch also stores attr->ia_mode into inode->i_mode immediately; uid and gid in the request branch are not stored in the inode. For ATTR_SIZE: an encrypted inode shrunk to a size not a multiple of the fscrypt block size is always done by the request (with the fscrypt RMW data, to be filled later); otherwise, if !do_sync and FILE_EXCL is issued and the new size is not smaller, a larger size is written to the inode locally (i_size, blocks, reported size, FILE_EXCL dirtied) and ATTR_MTIME is added to ia_valid, an equal size does nothing; otherwise, if FILE_SHARED is not issued or the size differs (this includes any shrink), the size goes into the request. ATTR_MTIME follows the same pattern as atime. ATTR_CTIME, only when none of size, mtime, atime, mode, uid, gid is in ia_valid (after the size step may have added mtime), dirties AUTH_EXCL, else FILE_EXCL, else XATTR_EXCL if issued, and otherwise puts the ctime into the request; ATTR_FILE only logs. If any caps were dirtied it marks them dirty (__ceph_mark_dirty_caps), sets the inode ctime from attr->ia_ctime and increments the inode version. It then restricts the caps to release to those issued, drops i_ceph_lock and snap_rwsem if held, and marks the inode dirty if the cap marking asked for it. If the request mask is non-zero it gives the request a reference on the inode (ihold) and sends it with ceph_mdsc_do_request (an fscrypt_truncate fill failure is returned as the error instead, without sending); if the MDS answers -EAGAIN and the retry counter (20) is not exhausted it puts the request, frees the cap flush and restarts from the retry label (the alias and access check are not repeated). At the exit it puts the request, frees the cap flush and, if the result is non-negative and the mask included the size, runs __ceph_do_pending_vmtruncate. It returns 0 on success (including when nothing had to be sent), or the negative errno (the MDS result or one of the errors above).
note: Reviewer right: inode.c ATTR_MODE else-if branch (about 2704-2710) does inode->i_mode = attr->ia_mode before putting mode in the request. Also rewrote the fscrypt_auth three-way case (identical value + shared issued does nothing, cia->fscrypt_auth set NULL in all three, not set NULL in the -EINVAL exits), size branches (equal size under FILE_EXCL no-op, shrink goes to request), and ctime cap choice.

name: de_thread
prose: Precondition: tsk is the current task, about to complete an exec, and tsk->signal and tsk->sighand are valid; the caller holds no siglock or tasklist_lock and may sleep. Postcondition: returns 0 or -EAGAIN. If the thread group has only tsk (thread_group_empty) it just sets tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD (and BUG_ONs if tsk is not the group leader) and returns 0 without touching sig->group_exec_task or notify_count. Otherwise, under the sighand siglock: if the group is already exiting (SIGNAL_GROUP_EXIT) or another task is already exec-ing (sig->group_exec_task non-NULL) it returns -EAGAIN with no state changed; else it sets sig->group_exec_task = tsk, kills all other threads (zap_other_threads) and sets notify_count to the number of threads to wait for (one less if tsk is not the leader, since the leader is waited for separately), then sleeps killably until notify_count reaches 0. If a fatal signal becomes pending during either wait (waiting for the other threads, or for the old leader to become a zombie) it takes tasklist_lock for reading, resets sig->group_exec_task = NULL and sig->notify_count = 0, releases the lock and returns -EAGAIN (the state it set is unwound; other threads may already have been killed). If tsk was not the group leader it then waits for the old leader to exit (looping with tasklist_lock for writing and the cgroup threadgroup lock held, notify_count set to -1); once the leader has an exit state, still under tasklist_lock (write) and the cgroup threadgroup lock, it takes over the leader's start_time/start_boottime, swaps tids with it (exchange_tids), transfers its TGID, PGID and SID pids, replaces it in the tasks and sibling lists, becomes the group leader with exit_signal SIGCHLD (the old leader gets exit_signal -1, is BUG_ON-checked to be EXIT_ZOMBIE, and is marked EXIT_DEAD, waking its tracer if ptraced). It then drops tasklist_lock and the cgroup threadgroup lock, and only after that calls release_task() on the old leader. On success (both for leader and non-leader callers in a multi-thread group) it resets sig->group_exec_task = NULL and sig->notify_count = 0, sets tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD, and returns 0 with tsk the sole thread and group leader and no lock held.
note: Reviewer right: exec.c:1019-1025 write_unlock_irq(&tasklist_lock); cgroup_threadgroup_change_end(tsk); then release_task(leader). Also thread_group_empty path does not reset group_exec_task/notify_count (no_thread_group label, exec.c about 1030), notify_count is decremented for a non-leader, and the leader wait loop sets notify_count=-1.

name: bfq_bfqq_expire
prose: Precondition: bfqd is the bfq_data whose in-service queue is bfqq, compensate says whether to compensate for idle-time overestimation, reason is a valid expiration cause, and the caller holds the bfq_data lock. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It computes slow with bfq_bfqq_is_slow(bfqd, bfqq, compensate, &delta); delta starts at 0 and is overwritten (in milliseconds of service time) only when bfqq is a sync queue, otherwise slow is false and delta stays 0. If bfqq->wr_coeff == 1 and (slow, or reason == BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT with budget left >= entity->budget / 3), the queue is charged delta (time) instead of service via bfq_bfqq_charge_time. If bfqd->low_latency and wr_coeff == 1, last_wr_start_finish is set to jiffies. If bfqd->low_latency, bfqd->bfq_wr_max_softrt_rate > 0 and bfqq->sort_list is empty: soft_rt_next_start is recomputed with bfq_bfqq_softrt_next_start when bfqq->dispatched == 0, else if dispatched > 0 the softrt_update flag is marked. bfqd->rqs_injected and bfqd->wait_dispatch are set to false and bfqd->waited_rq to NULL. The budget is recomputed with __bfq_bfqq_recalc_budget(bfqd, bfqq, reason) and the queue expired with __bfq_bfqq_expire; if that returns true (bfqq gone) the function returns at once without touching any service counter. Otherwise: if bfqq is not busy and reason is neither BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT nor BFQQE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED the queue is marked non_blocking_wait_rq and bfqq->entity.service is kept, else bfqq->entity.service is set to 0; in both cases the service field of every parent entity (entity->parent, then upward through for_each_entity: all ancestors with CONFIG_BFQ_GROUP_IOSCHED, a single level otherwise) is then set to 0. No lock or reference is acquired or released by this function itself.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. bfq-iosched.c:4431-4450 the code ends with entity = entity->parent; for_each_entity(entity) entity->service = 0; (parent counters ARE reset). Prose tightened: delta stays 0 for non-sync queue (4156), ancestors via for_each_entity (bfq-iosched.h:1105,1123).

name: BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS(inode_size, struct btrfs_inode_item, size, 64)
prose: Generated pair of inline accessors for the 64-bit size field of struct btrfs_inode_item: btrfs_inode_size(eb, s) and btrfs_set_inode_size(eb, s, val); the name field is the macro invocation that generates them. Precondition: eb is a valid extent buffer; s is the offset of an inode item within eb (an offset cast to a pointer, not a real address). Postcondition: btrfs_inode_size returns btrfs_get_64(eb, s, offsetof(struct btrfs_inode_item, size)): the little-endian 64-bit size stored in the item, or 0 after a bounds warning if the field lies outside eb->len. btrfs_set_inode_size stores val little-endian in that field through btrfs_set_64, and writes nothing (with a bounds warning) if the field lies outside eb->len. Neither takes a lock or reference; the getter does not modify the buffer.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. accessors.h:62-74 macro and accessors.c DEFINE_BTRFS_SETGET_BITS: bounds check returns 0 / writes nothing after report_setget_bounds.

name: btrfs_init_new_device
prose: Function btrfs_init_new_device(fs_info, device_path): add the block device at device_path as a new writeable device of the mounted filesystem. Precondition: fs_info is a mounted btrfs filesystem; the caller holds no lock that the function takes (s_umount, uuid_mutex, device_list_mutex, chunk_mutex); it may sleep. Early failures, in order, with no change to the filesystem: -EROFS if the superblock is read-only and fs_devices->seeding is not set; the error of bdev_file_open_by_path (open for write with fs_holder_ops); -EINVAL if btrfs_check_device_zone_type fails; -EINVAL if the device size is not larger than BTRFS_DEVICE_RANGE_RESERVED (the opened block device reference is dropped with bdev_fput on these). Then, if fs_devices->seeding is set, it takes s_umount for writing and then uuid_mutex and keeps both until just after the first transaction commit (the point where it releases them for the seeding case); it calls sync_blockdev; it returns -EEXIST if a device with the same block device is already in fs_devices->devices; it allocates a device (btrfs_alloc_device error returned), sets the device bdev, looks up devt (lookup_bdev error), gets zone info (btrfs_get_dev_zone_info error) and starts a transaction on the dev root (its error returned). Failures in these steps free what was set up (device, zone info) and call bdev_fput, and release uuid_mutex and s_umount if they were taken. It then initialises the device (writeable, sizes from the block device rounded to the sector size, blocksize set), and for a seeding filesystem calls btrfs_init_sprout (on error: abort the transaction, end it, free zone info and device, bdev_fput, unlock, return the error). Under device_list_mutex and chunk_mutex it sprouts the seed devices (seeding only), adds the device to fs_devices->devices and alloc_list, increments num_devices, open_devices, rw_devices and total_devices, adds the device size to total_rw_bytes and free_chunk_space, may set rotating, increases the superblock total bytes and device count, clears the space info full flags and adds the sysfs device entry. For seeding it then calls init_first_rw_device under chunk_mutex. It then calls btrfs_add_dev_item and, for seeding, btrfs_finish_sprout and btrfs_sysfs_update_sprout_fsid. If init_first_rw_device, btrfs_add_dev_item or btrfs_finish_sprout fails, the transaction is aborted with that error and the rollback below is done. The first btrfs_commit_transaction is then called. Non-seeding case: its result ret is not rolled back on failure; the function goes on to btrfs_forget_devices(device->devt) and update_dev_time(device_path) and returns ret (0 on success, the commit error otherwise). Seeding case: uuid_mutex and s_umount are released right after the first commit; if that commit failed its error is returned at once (no rollback, no forget, no time update); otherwise btrfs_relocate_sys_chunks is called (its failure is only reported through btrfs_handle_fs_error and does not change the return value), then btrfs_attach_transaction: if that returns -ENOENT the function returns 0 immediately (skipping forget and time update); if it fails with another error it takes the rollback path with that error (the transaction handle is not ended again); else the second btrfs_commit_transaction result becomes ret, and the function then does btrfs_forget_devices and update_dev_time and returns ret. Rollback path (error_sysfs): removes the sysfs entry, takes device_list_mutex and chunk_mutex, unlinks the device from the lists, undoes the counters, free_chunk_space and superblock totals (restoring the saved original values), ends the transaction if one is held, destroys the zone info, frees the device, calls bdev_fput and releases uuid_mutex and s_umount only if still held; the error is returned.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. Reviewer right: volumes.c btrfs_init_new_device ~3030-3047: uuid_mutex/s_umount are released right after the first commit, before btrfs_relocate_sys_chunks and the second commit; also failure rollbacks after the first commit, ENOENT return 0, and commit failure in non-seeding case not rolled back.

name: aio_poll_wake
prose: Precondition: wait is the wait-queue entry embedded in the poll_iocb of a live aio_kiocb; the caller holds the waitqueue lock (head->lock); key is the poll key (may be NULL, giving mask 0). Postcondition: returns 0 with no effect if mask is nonzero and shares no bit with req->events. Otherwise returns 1 and does one of: (a) completes inline when mask != 0, req->work_scheduled is false and spin_trylock_irqsave(ctx_lock) succeeds: removes the entry from the waitqueue, removes the iocb from ctx->active_reqs, sets ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), and then drops the iocb reference with iocb_put after releasing ctx_lock, except that if an eventfd is attached and eventfd_signal_allowed() is false the put is deferred to a scheduled aio_poll_put_work; or (b) otherwise (mask == 0, work already scheduled or trylock failed): schedules req->work and sets work_scheduled if it was not set, else sets work_need_resched; and if mask has POLLFREE in this branch it also sets req->cancelled, removes the entry from the waitqueue and, as the last step, publishes req->head = NULL with a release store. POLLFREE is not specially handled on the inline path.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. Verified aio.c aio_poll_wake line by line (mask/events check, trylock inline path incl. eventfd deferral, else-branch scheduling, POLLFREE cancel/list_del_init/smp_store_release as last step).

name: aio_poll
prose: Precondition: aiocb is an initialised aio_kiocb (ki_ctx valid, poll.file set) and iocb is the kernel copy of the user control block for IOCB_CMD_POLL; the caller holds no ctx_lock. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (before touching the poll request) if iocb->aio_buf has bits above the low 16, or aio_offset, aio_nbytes or aio_rw_flags is nonzero. Otherwise it initialises the poll request (events = demangle_poll(aio_buf) | EPOLLERR | EPOLLHUP), calls vfs_poll with a queueing callback, takes ctx->ctx_lock (irq-disabling) and returns apt.error, which is 0 or -EINVAL. Cases: (1) the file registered no waitqueue: if an event of the request was ready, ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), the iocb reference is dropped with iocb_put and 0 is returned (completed synchronously); if none was ready -EINVAL is returned and the caller keeps the iocb reference. (2) the file registered exactly one waitqueue (apt.error 0): if the request was already removed from the waitqueue, or aio_poll_wake already scheduled the completion work, an already-done or in-progress completion is assumed, mask is ignored and the function returns 0 (when the request is still on the queue with work scheduled, it is also added to ctx->active_reqs with ki_cancel = aio_poll_cancel; when it was removed from the queue nothing more is done); otherwise, if an event was ready, the wait entry is removed from the waitqueue, ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), the iocb reference is dropped and 0 is returned; otherwise the request is added to ctx->active_reqs with ki_cancel = aio_poll_cancel and 0 is returned. (3) the file registered more than one waitqueue (apt.error = -EINVAL): if the request was no longer on its first queue or completion work was already scheduled, req->cancelled is set and 0 is returned; otherwise (still on the first queue, no work scheduled) the wait entry is removed and, if an event was ready, the request is completed synchronously (ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), iocb_put, return 0), else -EINVAL is returned and the caller keeps the iocb reference. ctx_lock and the waitqueue lock are released before returning.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. aio.c aio_poll l.~1900-1945: multi-queue case (apt.error=-EINVAL, queued) with an event ready (mask != 0, on_queue, no work) completes synchronously and returns 0, not -EINVAL; prose did not say mask must be 0. Rest verified.

name: __io_submit_one
prose: Precondition: req is a freshly allocated aio_kiocb belonging to ctx, iocb is the kernel copy of the user iocb, user_iocb its user address, compat the layout flag. Postcondition: returns -EBADF if fget(iocb->aio_fildes) fails (req->ki_filp is NULL, no reference taken); if IOCB_FLAG_RESFD is set and eventfd_ctx_fdget fails returns that error (PTR_ERR) with req->ki_filp holding a file reference; returns -EFAULT if writing KIOCB_KEY to user_iocb->aio_key fails (req->ki_filp, and req->ki_eventfd if set, hold references); otherwise it fills req->ki_res (obj, data, res = 0, res2 = 0) and returns the result of the handler for iocb->aio_lio_opcode: aio_read (PREAD, PREADV), aio_write (PWRITE, PWRITEV), aio_fsync (FSYNC with datasync false, FDSYNC with true) or aio_poll (POLL). Those handlers return 0 (the request completed or will be completed asynchronously) or a negative errno (they never return -EIOCBQUEUED to this function: aio_read and aio_write absorb it); any other opcode returns -EINVAL. This function does not itself release the file or eventfd references: they stay in req and are released when req is destroyed, which the caller (io_submit_one) does via iocb_destroy (and returns the slot with put_reqs_available) when the return value is nonzero; when the return is 0 the request is complete or will be completed asynchronously and the async machinery owns req and its references.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. aio.c:1581-1650: aio_read/aio_write/aio_fsync never return -EIOCBQUEUED (aio_rw_done consumes it, they return 0 or errno); aio_poll returns 0/-EINVAL; io_submit_one at aio.c:2023-2064 does iocb_put then iocb_destroy+put_reqs_available on nonzero.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_submit, aio_context_t, ctx_id, long, nr,
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_submit(ctx_id, nr, iocbpp). Precondition: iocbpp is a user pointer to an array of nr user iocb pointers. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if nr < 0 or lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) finds no context.
