Otherwise it clamps nr to ctx->nr_events, brackets the loop with blk_start_plug/blk_finish_plug when nr > AIO_PLUG_THRESHOLD, and submits the iocbs one at a time with io_submit_one(ctx, user_iocb, false) until one fails. Stopping at index i (0 <= i <= nr, i being the number submitted successfully), it returns i if i > 0, otherwise the first error: -EFAULT if the iocb pointer could not be read from user memory, or the error of io_submit_one (e.g. -EFAULT, -EINVAL, -EAGAIN, -EBADF, or a handler error), or 0 if nothing was attempted (nr == 0 after clamping). The context reference from lookup_ioctx is dropped before returning on every path after the lookup.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. aio.c SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_submit): nr<0 -> -EINVAL; lookup_ioctx; clamp to nr_events; plug if > AIO_PLUG_THRESHOLD; return i ? i : ret; percpu_ref_put(&ctx->users) on all paths after lookup

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_cancel, aio_context_t, ctx_id, struct iocb __user *, iocb,
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_cancel(ctx_id, iocb, result). Precondition: iocb is a user pointer to a previously submitted control block; result is unused. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if iocb->aio_key cannot be read, -EINVAL if the key is not KIOCB_KEY or lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) finds no context (no reference taken). Otherwise, under ctx->ctx_lock it searches ctx->active_reqs for the request whose ki_res.obj equals the iocb address; if found it calls its ki_cancel callback, removes it from the active list (list_del_init) and uses the callback's return; if not found the result stays -EINVAL. A callback return of 0 is converted to -EINPROGRESS (the completion event is delivered through the ring, not via result); any other callback return value (non-zero) is returned unchanged. The context reference is dropped before returning.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. aio.c SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_cancel) l.~2200-2240 verified: get_user->-EFAULT, key!=KIOCB_KEY->-EINVAL, lookup fail -EINVAL, ki_cancel under ctx_lock, 0->-EINPROGRESS, percpu_ref_put.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(io_getevents, aio_context_t, ctx_id,
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout) (CONFIG_64BIT). Precondition: events is a user buffer for up to nr struct io_event; timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user struct __kernel_timespec giving a relative timeout. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and get_timespec64 fails (it fails only when the copy from user faults). Otherwise it calls do_io_getevents (timeout NULL means wait indefinitely, KTIME_MAX): that returns -EINVAL if ctx_id does not name a context, or if min_nr < 0 or min_nr > nr, and otherwise the result of read_events: the number of events copied to the user buffer (0 or fewer than min_nr if the timeout expired or a signal interrupted the wait; a timeout or interrupted wait does not itself produce an error from read_events), or a negative errno (-EFAULT if copying to the user buffer faulted, -EINVAL if the context is dead) which is returned only when no event had been copied yet. The result is stored in an int; if it is 0 and a signal is pending it is replaced by -EINTR. The context reference taken by do_io_getevents is dropped. The ring head is advanced past the events copied by each successful ring read; a faulting copy leaves that read's events unconsumed.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. Corrected: aio.c read_events (1312-1367) breaks out on ret2 (-ETIME/-ERESTARTSYS) but returns ret (count), so an interrupted wait is not a negative errno from read_events; errors from aio_read_events (1294-1305) are stored in *i only if *i == 0. get_timespec64 (time.c:872) fails only with -EFAULT.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_pgetevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout, usig). Precondition: events is a user buffer for up to nr io_events; timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user __kernel_timespec; usig, if non-NULL, points to a user __aio_sigset. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if timeout cannot be copied or if usig cannot be copied; otherwise calls set_user_sigmask(ksig.sigmask, ksig.sigsetsize) (a NULL usig gives a NULL mask) and returns its non-zero error (e.g. -EINVAL for a wrong sigsetsize, -EFAULT) without waiting. On success of that it waits for events with do_io_getevents (result: number of events read, or -EINVAL for bad ctx_id or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a read_events error), then records whether a signal is pending and calls restore_saved_sigmask_unless(interrupted), which restores the caller's original signal mask unless a signal is pending (in which case it is restored on signal delivery). If interrupted and the result is 0 it returns -ERESTARTNOHAND; otherwise it returns the result.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. aio.c io_pgetevents ~2283-2305 + set_user_sigmask (signal.c:3354) verified.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents_time32
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_pgetevents_time32(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout, usig), compiled only for 32-bit with CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME. Precondition: timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user struct old_timespec32 (relative); usig, if non-NULL, points to a user struct __aio_sigset. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if the timeout or the sigset cannot be copied from user; returns the non-zero error of set_user_sigmask (e.g. -EINVAL for a bad sigsetsize) before waiting; otherwise waits for events with do_io_getevents (number of events read, -EINVAL for a bad context or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a read_events error), restores the saved signal mask unless a signal is pending (restore_saved_sigmask_unless), and returns -ERESTARTNOHAND if a signal is pending and the result is 0, else the result.
note: re-review only (first review call failed); prose unchanged from redo-A. Verified aio.c 2292-2445 io_pgetevents_time32: get_old_timespec32/copy_from_user -> -EFAULT, set_user_sigmask error returned before waiting, do_io_getevents, restore_saved_sigmask_unless(interrupted), -ERESTARTNOHAND if interrupted && !ret.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(io_getevents_time32, __u32, ctx_id,
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_getevents_time32(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout) (CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME). Precondition: timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user struct old_timespec32 (relative). Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and cannot be copied; otherwise the result of do_io_getevents (events copied: 0 or fewer than min_nr on timeout, -EINVAL for an invalid context or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a read_events error), stored in an int, with a result of 0 replaced by -EINTR when a signal is pending.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents,
prose: Generated compat syscall compat_sys_io_pgetevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout, usig) (CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME). Precondition: timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user struct old_timespec32; usig, if non-NULL, points to a user struct __compat_aio_sigset. name: cow_file_range
prose: Precondition: inode is a btrfs inode, [start, end] is a delalloc range whose data space is reserved and whose extent bits are locked by the caller, locked_folio is NULL or the locked folio covering the start of the range, done_offset is NULL or a valid pointer, flags is a combination of COW_FILE_RANGE_* flags, and the range length (aligned to sectorsize, at least one sector) does not exceed the filesystem total bytes (only asserted). Postcondition: for a free-space inode it returns -EINVAL after the error cleanup below (nothing was reserved, so only the delalloc/lock bits of the whole range are cleared and the data reservation released). Unless COW_FILE_RANGE_NO_INLINE is set it first calls cow_file_range_inline: a result of 0 is returned as 1 (the range was written inline and the IO and cleanup are already done), a negative result is returned unchanged (cow_file_range_inline has already cleaned up), both jumping to done, which sets *done_offset = end when done_offset is non-NULL and returns; a positive result (inline not possible) continues with the normal path. Otherwise it loops, reserving an extent with btrfs_reserve_extent (exact size, at least min_alloc_size), and for each reserved extent locks that extent range, creates the io extent map and an ordered extent, (for the data relocation root clones csums into the ordered extent with btrfs_reloc_clone_csums), advancing start; on the zoned -EAGAIN case it waits for a zone to finish and retries when still at the original start, otherwise with done_offset non-NULL it shortens end to start - 1 and ends the loop with 0, and with done_offset NULL it fails with -ENOSPC. After the loop it clears LOCKED and DELALLOC over [orig_start, end], applies PAGE_UNLOCK (unless COW_FILE_RANGE_KEEP_LOCKED) and PAGE_SET_ORDERED to the folios, and returns 0 through done (setting *done_offset = end if done_offset is non-NULL). On a failure after the setup the function returns the negative errno after the error cleanup (it logs an error with btrfs_err, never writes *done_offset, and calls mapping_set_error on the inode mapping when some part before start was already processed and locked_folio is NULL). The cleanup depends on where it failed: (a) btrfs_reserve_extent fails (other than the handled -EAGAIN) or -ENOSPC from -EAGAIN: nothing to undo for the current extent; (b) btrfs_create_io_em fails: the extent range is unlocked, the block group reservation is dropped and the reserved extent is freed; (c) btrfs_alloc_ordered_extent fails: the range is unlocked, the extent map range is dropped, then as (b); (d) btrfs_reloc_clone_csums fails: the extent map range is dropped, the ordered extent reference is put and the block group reservation is dropped, start is advanced past this extent, but the reserved extent is NOT freed here (it belongs to the ordered extent, whose cleanup is part of cleaning up [orig_start, start)). In all failure cases it then cleans up the ordered extents for [orig_start, start) and clears LOCKED and DELALLOC and ends writeback on those folios, for the current extent (cases b and c) clears the bits, unlocks the folios and frees its data qgroup reservation, and for the untouched rest (when start + cur_alloc_size < end) also clears the bits including the data reservation, unlocks the folios and frees its data qgroup reservation.

Also added positive-return-of-cow_file_range_inline fall-through and per-failure cleanup differences.

name: btrfs_finish_one_ordered
prose: Precondition: ordered_extent is a valid ordered extent whose IO has completed (data written or failed) and not yet completed here; the caller owns one reference and the ordered tree owns another. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and a negative errno on failure; the possible errors are -EIO when BTRFS_ORDERED_IOERR was already set, an error from btrfs_zone_finish_endio, from joining the transaction, from btrfs_insert_raid_extent, -EINVAL for a NOCOW ordered extent still linked on its csum list, or an error from btrfs_mark_extent_written, insert_ordered_extent_file_extent, btrfs_unpin_extent_cache, add_pending_csums or btrfs_update_inode_fallback. Steps: if the extent was truncated to length 0 it goes straight to the common exit with result 0 and nothing inserted. For a non-NOCOW extent (COW, PREALLOC, DIRECT or ENCODED) it locks the range (EXTENT_LOCKED | EXTENT_FINISHING_ORDERED) before joining a transaction (the free-space transaction join is used for a free-space inode). Once a transaction is joined, every failure aborts it (the early -EIO, zone-finish, truncated-to-zero and join-failure paths have no transaction to abort). Success for a NOCOW extent: after the raid-extent insert and the csum-list check it only writes the safe disk i_size and updates the inode item (btrfs_update_inode_fallback); no file extent item is inserted, no extent cache is unpinned and no checksums are added. Success for a non-NOCOW extent: for a PREALLOC extent the range is marked written (btrfs_mark_extent_written), otherwise the file extent item is inserted (and the reserved extent is considered consumed, the delalloc bytes of the block group are released); then the extent cache is unpinned, pending checksums are added, EXTENT_DELALLOC_NEW | EXTENT_ADD_INODE_BYTES is cleared for the range when applicable (not DIRECT/ENCODED/PREALLOC and not truncated), the safe disk i_size is written and the inode item is updated. Common exit: the extent bits of the range (EXTENT_DEFRAG, plus LOCKED and FINISHING_ORDERED when they were taken and DELALLOC_NEW where it applies) are cleared and the transaction, if any, is ended. Then, if the result is non-zero or the extent was truncated: on failure BTRFS_ORDERED_IOERR is set on the ordered extent (btrfs_mark_ordered_extent_error); the extent map range not written (the whole range, or the part after the truncated length) is dropped unless the inode is a free-space inode; and when (failure or truncated to length 0), the file extent was not already inserted and the ordered extent is neither NOCOW nor PREALLOC, the reserved extent is returned to the allocator (discarded first if the discard=sync option is on and it failed) and the data qgroup reservation is freed. In every case, even on failure, the ordered extent is removed from the inode and root lists, remaining bio cs lists are cleaned up, and both references (the tree and the caller) are dropped, so the caller must not use ordered_extent afterwards.

name: afs_select_vlserver
prose: Precondition: vc was initialised by afs_begin_vlserver_operation (nr_iterations starts at -1); on calls after the first, vc->call_error and vc->call_abort_code hold the outcome of the previous call and vc->alist and vc->server_list hold the references acquired by earlier calls; single-threaded per cursor. Postcondition: always increments vc->nr_iterations first. Then, if AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is already set, it returns false with nothing else changed. On the first call (nr_iterations == 0) it starts iteration (afs_start_vl_iteration: may wait for a DNS lookup; errors -ERESTARTSYS, -ENOENT, -EDESTADDRREQ recorded in cumul_error; an empty server list returns false without setting an error and leaves the server_list reference held) and sends probes (an error is recorded in cumul_error). A failure in either step ends as a failure return (see below). On later calls it first writes call_error to the used address's last_error and evaluates it: error 0 or any error not listed below: cumul_error.error = error, sets STOP and returns false, leaving the vc->alist and vc->server_list references for afs_end_vlserver_operation to release; -ECONNABORTED with abort code AFSVL_IO, AFSVL_BADVOLOPER or AFSVL_NOMEM records -EREMOTEIO and moves to the next server, any other abort code is recorded (afs_prioritise_error) and the cursor fails; connection errors (-ERFKILL, -EADDRNOTAVAIL, -ENETUNREACH, -EHOSTUNREACH, -EHOSTDOWN, -ECONNREFUSED, -ETIMEDOUT, -ETIME) are recorded and the next untried responding address of the same server is tried (or, if none remains, the next server); -ECONNRESET is recorded, sets AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY and goes to the next server; -EOPNOTSUPP goes to the next server without recording an error. Moving to the next server first updates alist->preferred if the last call responded on a different address whose preferred address was tried, and drops the alist reference. Server choice waits for probes (an error from afs_wait_for_vl_probes is recorded and the cursor fails), then picks the preferred server if untried, else the untried responding server with the lowest probe rtt (the last one among equals); if none is left it restarts once from the beginning when RETRY is set (dropping the old alist and server_list references; a second restart fails without recording more) or, when RETRY is not set, records the probe errors of all servers and fails. Returns true when an address has been selected: vc->server, vc->server_index and vc->alist (a reference to the server's address list) are set, vc->addr_index is an address that responded, has not failed its probe and is not yet tried (the preferred one if available), that bit is set in vc->addr_tried and vc->call_responded is false. A false return after a failure also sets AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP and drops the vc->alist reference if one is held (updating alist->preferred as above), leaves the vc->server_list reference held for afs_end_vlserver_operation (it is NULL only after a restart dropped it), and the final error is in vc->cumul_error.

Also tightened: addr selection excludes probe_failed addresses (iterate_address), server_list may be NULL after a restart, connection errors fall to next server when no address left.
